correctness.rationale: Independent symbolic differentiation gives \(f_a'''(x)<0\) on \(a<x<1\), forcing the central symmetric Jensen gap to decrease strictly in mean. Its upper-mean endpoint is negative, and its lower-mean endpoint has the sign opposite \(G_a(d)=7d^2+(9a-3)d+a(3a-2)\). For \(a<2/3\), exactly one feasible positive root generates the radical threshold, with all equality cases handled; for \(a\ge2/3\), \(G_a\) is positive. The derivative of the threshold is strictly negative. The standalone delivered checker passed 33,560 finite diagnostic assertions and is not an infinite proof.

This claim: \(f_a(x)=x(x-a)\sqrt{1-x}\) for \(0<a<1\), equal two-point weights, and the sign of the central second difference over all feasible means and amplitudes.
Worner 1992 and Ruel–Ayres 1999 explain nonlinear averaging and rate summation but their accessible material does not state or furnish the Brière-I all-amplitude threshold.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The known Lactin optimal-law claim cannot imply this explicit Brière-I sign classification because it assumes another temperature-response family. A general monotone-curvature or Jensen statement also does not by itself determine the exact domain-crossing amplitude. The complete proof requires verifying Brière-I-specific strict decrease of the central difference and its precise lower endpoint polynomial. Earlier unavailable literature might contain an equivalent specialization, so priority remains conditional.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The two-temperature Jensen comparison is equivalent to the central second difference of the Brière-I curve. The exact sign on the entire feasible (mean, amplitude, threshold ratio) domain is much stronger than local curvature or generic Jensen observations: strict negative third derivative of this specific rate function and an exact boundary quadratic yield the nonlocal radical amplitude limit, with a unique zero in the mean for smaller amplitudes. The inspected texts do not derive or imply these Brière-I-specific constants without performing that analysis.

originality.rationale: The analytical Brière-I all-mean two-point amplitude ceiling and unique crossover are not entailed by the known Lactin-2 optimal-law classification, Worner/Ruel-Ayres generic Jensen statements, or the specific examined full-text thermal-model articles. Full-text gaps in earlier plausibly relevant works are explicitly recorded, so this is a same-model best-knowledge assessment rather than a claim of exhaustive historical uniqueness.
residual_risks: Complete Brière 1999, Worner 1992, and Estay 2013 online full texts and possible historical appendices were unavailable to this scientific comparison.

value.rationale: Brière-I is a natural insect-development curve. A closed-form global threshold in both temperature threshold ratio and fluctuation amplitude determines when symmetric excursions can ever be advantageous at any feasible mean, with a unique interior crossover below the critical amplitude. This supplies a structural and usable analytic benchmark beyond a local Jensen sign test; it is not a population or field-calibration theorem.
